newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila business leader says worst over for peso.
newsitem.headline: Manila business leader says worst over for peso.

text.p: The Philippine peso is set to stabilise at 27.50/28.50 to the dollar with the easing of speculation, Raul Concepcion, president of the Federation of Philippine Industries said on Monday.
"The worst is over on the speculative attack on the peso and we will see the peso to gradually begin to stabilise in the range of 27.5 to 28.5," Concepcion said in a statement.

"Exporters will now surrender their export proceeds as the current rate is higher than what we predicted and exporters can earn a higher yield on their funds compared to a time deposit abroad," he said.
He said exporters and domestic industries had earlier recommended to the government to allow the exchange rate to float with a target of 27.5/28 by the end of the year.
Over a week ago, the central bank effectively devalued the peso. -- Manila newsroom (63 2) 841-8937
